key_insight: For a natural class of nonconvex functions, learning-rate decay lets SGD reach global optima with exponentially fewer gradient queries than any fixed learning rate in the small-step-size regime.
engineering_relevance: The result provides theoretical support for decaying learning rates when designing SGD-based global optimization workflows.
method: Analyze SGD with learning-rate decay on a natural class of nonconvex objectives.
Prove an exponential gradient-query advantage over fixed-rate SGD in the small-step-size regime.
Use weak Poincaré inequalities to show polynomial-time annealing for the associated non-logconcave sampling task.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical guarantees for a function class containing many popular nonconvex benchmarks, but gives no numerical evaluation results.
watch_item: The advantage is established for a specific function class and small-step-size regime, not arbitrary nonconvex objectives or practical training schedules.
paper_title: Learning Rate Decay Can Exponentially Accelerate SGD for Global Optimization of Nonconvex Functions
